intro: Real estate brokers negotiate, persuade and manage deals, skills prized across finance and sales. The closest of the 25 careers below is Securities, Commodities, and Financial Services Sales Agents, with an 88% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $78,660, which is 7% more than the $73,220 brokers earn.
why_it_works: Closing a sale means reading both sides, managing a timeline and keeping clients calm when a deal wobbles. O*NET rates negotiation at 4.12 out of 5 for brokers, one of the highest scores for any sales job, and persuasion at 3.88. Lending, financial sales and property management use the same strengths. Every match needs no new degree. The gaps are financial analysis and managing resources.
tips: Your closed deals are your resume: list volume, average price and how many transactions you managed each year.
Sales Managers are an 82% match and earn $148,270, which is 102% more.
Loan officer work keeps you in real estate with a median of $76,690 and a steadier pay pattern.

faq.q: What jobs can former real estate brokers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are financial services sales agents (88%), Loan Officers (85%) and property and community association managers (82%), based on O*NET 31.0. Property managers earn $69,990, which is 4% less than the $73,220 broker median, but offer steadier monthly income.

faq.q: Which careers for real estate brokers pay more?
faq.a: 15 of the 25 matches pay more than brokerage. Marketing Managers earn $166,790 (128% more), Financial Managers $166,570 (127% more) and Sales Managers $148,270 (102% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. These manager jobs usually expect years of experience leading a team.

faq.q: Do real estate brokers need another degree to switch?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches usually need no more education than brokers already have. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 55% of workers in the closest match, but licenses, such as securities registrations, often matter more than degrees in finance.

faq.q: What skills should real estate brokers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are systems analysis, managing materials, systems evaluation and managing financial resources. Judgment already rates 3.5 out of 5 for brokers in O*NET, so the step is mostly deeper financial analysis rather than better selling.
